build_note: Installed from pinned pure-Python py3-none-any wheels by hash (--no-deps). The image checks that the pydns/ and pystructs/ packages of the pydns3 0.0.10 and pystructs3 0.0.8 wheels are byte-identical to their pinned sdists, that both declare the MIT licence classifier, and that the codec sources and LICENSE files match recorded SHA-256 values.
dependencies_note: Only the modules that pydns.Message imports are installed: pystructs3 0.0.8 (the same author's struct library that holds the Domain name codec), pyderive3 0.0.8 (the same author's dataclass helper) and typing-extensions 4.16.0. pypool3 and pyserve3, which pydns3 requires only for its client and server modules, are not installed (pyserve3 is sdist-only); importing pydns does not import them. atheris 3.1.0 is the in-process fuzz bridge only.
parser_family: pydns3 (message.py Message.unpack, answer.py Answer.unpack, content.py typed RDATA classes, flags.py) over pystructs3 (struct.py Struct, std.py Domain name compression codec), both by Andrew C Scott
api: pydns.Message.unpack(local DNS message bytes) -> Message (id, Flags, questions, answers, authority, additional with typed A/AAAA/CNAME/MX content)
coverage: Python line tracing of the installed pydns package (parser lines) and of pystructs (underlying struct and Domain name codec, reported separately) during valid-control replay; Atheris import instrumentation for the byte-input bridge
scope: One RFC 1035 DNS message from local bytes via pydns.Message.unpack (the packet-parsing example of the README): header flags (pydns.Flags keeps AD and CD but drops the reserved Z bit, so z carries AD and CD only), questions, and CNAME/A/AAAA/MX answers with compressed names decoded by pystructs Domain; valid response and query controls only. RDATA values are the fields of the typed content objects (ip, name, preference, exchange); the harness decodes the ASCII name bytes, lower-cases them and adds the trailing dot, and prints the ipaddress values with str. The client and server modules are not imported.
